summary: Prolonged handshake latency and intermittent 504s for chat completions after runtime affinity rollout
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (TempoHealth) report elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completions starting immediately after a staged runtime affinity rollout on 2026-03-12. In many sessions the request either delays first token emission by 3–8s or ultimately returns a 504 timeout within the customer app, primarily for short prompts and bursty traffic.

Impact:
- Multiple production accounts (enterprise tier) see degraded user experience in chat widgets (slow initial response or 504s).
- Affects short/prompt-heavy flows used by TempoHealth clinical triage (increased abandonment).
- Estimated 12% of chat requests during the rollout window returned 504 or had TTFB > 2s.

Environment:
- Prod environment: us-west-2, Redwood hosted API
- Runtime rolled: runtime-2.2.0-beta (affinity/kernel-selection changes) deployed 2026-03-12 03:40 UTC (canary then ramped)
- Model variants: redwood-2x pinned to v2026-02 by customer

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Send short chat prompt (~8 tokens user prompt + system prompt) to chat completions endpoint pinned to redwood-2x@v2026-02 with streaming=true.
2) Perform bursts of 40 concurrent sessions from a single region for ~30s.
3) Observe initial token delay or 504 at ~2–6s.

Observed logs and traces:
- Sample request IDs from TempoHealth: req_usw_3a8f7e, req_usw_3a8f92, req_usw_3a9a10 (attached).
- Console traces show first_byte_latency spiking from baseline 120ms to 1.8s median for affected traces and 95th percentile up to 5s.
- Traces show additional serialization/compilation time in the serving-runtime hot path for small sequence lengths (cold kernel selection), and increased queue time on dispatcher nodes.
- Metrics around KV cache hits show a drop during the rollout window for these traces.

Expected behavior:
- First token emitted within ~200–400ms for small prompts under normal load.

Actual behavior:
- First token delayed 1–5+ seconds or request returns 504; streaming does not begin until after the delay when it succeeds.

Attachments provided by customer:
- Three request traces, client-side timeout logs, and example prompt payloads.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:05 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged. Hi TempoHealth — thanks for the report and samples. We're triaging immediately and have opened INC-20260312-07. Can you confirm whether you pinned runtime or allowed auto-upgrades? Also sending a couple of request IDs back to us is very helpful (we have the ones attached).

2026-03-12 10:21 UTC - TempoHealth (Customer): We did not pin runtime; we only pinned the model to v2026-02. The issue started exactly after your 2.2.0-beta rollout. Attaching two additional request IDs from our logs.

2026-03-12 12:00 UTC - Arjun Patel (SRE): Reproduced locally with synthetic load targeting short prompts. Evidence suggests kernel-selection path introduced in runtime-2.2.0-beta is triggering cold compilations for small sequence lengths which increases per-request latency. Also seeing dispatcher queuing increase under bursty small-req workloads. Temporary mitigation: rolling back affinity on a subset of nodes and prewarmed instances appears to reduce TTFB.

2026-03-13 02:14 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Shared mitigation steps with TempoHealth (pin runtime to runtime-2.1.4 or request tenant routing to avoid updated pool). Customer reports partial improvement but still sees intermittent 504s during high concurrency windows.

2026-03-14 09:30 UTC - Arjun Patel (SRE): Creating a hotfix PR to skip JIT-kernel selection for short sequences and to increase prewarm budget for affected pools. Refer PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421. Keeping this ticket open while patch is validated in canary.
investigation_notes: Can reproduce with short prompts and high concurrency; not observed with long-form generation workloads.
Profiler traces show ~1.2s spent in kernel selection + compilation path on affected nodes; previous runtime had this path at ~40–80ms for same traces.
KV-cache hit rate dropped during rollout for affected request IDs suggesting cache warming regressions tied to new affinity routing.
Dispatcher queue depth increases under bursts due to affinity shards receiving disproportionate short-req load (hot-shard syndrome).
No increase in GPU OOMs or host-level resource saturation observed; issue appears software-path related (compiler/selection and routing imbalance).
Related internal ticket INT-4123 opened to look at scheduler/routing heuristic changes in runtime-2.2.0-beta.
resolution: Temporary mitigations applied 2026-03-12: rollback affinity changes on 30% of serving pool for us-west-2, increase prewarm nodes for short-prompt service class, and advised customer to pin runtime to runtime-2.1.4 if urgent (instructions provided).
Short-term: customer-side pin of runtime confirmed to reduce incidence by ~85% for their traffic pattern; monitoring in place.

Work in progress: hotfix PR (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421) to bypass JIT kernel selection for sequences < 64 tokens and to rebalance affinity heuristics. Patch is in canary verification as of 2026-03-14.

Follow-up actions: improve rollout canary metrics to include small-prompt TTFB and dispatcher queue depth, add automated prewarm triggers for affinity rebalancing, and schedule postmortem after full fix is deployed.
